key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 67
obligation: Internal audit should independently assess the review of material changes in validation methodology and/or processes, or process-related aspects of changes in the definition of default.
quote: the review of those aspects should be independently assessed by the internal audit function.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, para. 68
obligation: The institution should clearly document the responsibilities of its different internal control functions with respect to the independent assessment (e.g. definition of default, IT implementation of the rating system, assignment of exposures to exposure classes).
quote: institutions should clearly document the responsibilities of their different internal control functions with respect to the independent assessment

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 19.1
obligation: The institution shall add to its risk estimates a margin of conservatism related to the expected range of estimation errors.
quote: Institutions must add to their estimates a MoC that is related to the expected range of estimation errors.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 19.1
obligation: The institution should follow paragraphs 36 to 52 of the EBA Guidelines on PD and LGD when determining the MoC.
quote: institutions are expected to follow paragraphs 36 to 52 of the EBA Guidelines on PD and LGD.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 19.1
obligation: The institution shall reflect in the MoC the uncertainty at the level of the final risk estimates (grade or pool).
quote: The ECB understands that the MoC must reflect the uncertainty at the level of the final risk estimates (namely, at the level of the grade or pool).

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 19.1
obligation: The institution should be able to ensure monotonicity in its final estimates while still reflecting uncertainty at grade or pool level.
quote: institutions should be able to ensure monotonicity in their final estimates while still reflecting the uncertainty at grade or pool level.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 19.1
obligation: The institution should consider in the MoC any deficiencies stemming from missing or inaccurate information, including, where relevant and material, missing or inaccurate climate-related information.
quote: the MoC should consider any deficiencies stemming from missing or inaccurate information including, where relevant and material, any missing or inaccurate climate-related information considered in risk estimates.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution shall review its estimates whenever new information comes to light but at least on an annual basis.
quote: Institutions must review their estimates whenever new information comes to light but at least on an annual basis.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should have in place a framework for the review of estimates in line with paragraphs 217 to 221 of the EBA Guidelines on PD and LGD.
quote: they are expected to have in place a framework under paragraphs 217 to 221 of the EBA Guidelines on PD and LGD.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should perform the analysis of predictive power of PD models at grade level, or at a sufficient level of granularity where direct PD estimates are used.
quote: the analysis should be performed at grade level; for institutions using direct PD estimates, it should be performed at a sufficient level of granularity

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should use a range of metrics, including statistical tests and graphical analysis of the evolution of default rates and PD, to assess the predictive ability of PD models.
quote: institutions should use a range of metrics to assess predictive ability, including statistical tests and graphical analysis of the evolution of default rates and PD.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should run back-testing of LGD models combining different components (e.g. secured and unsecured) at both component and facility level.
quote: the back-testing analysis referred to in paragraph 218(c)(ii) of the EBA Guidelines on PD and LGD should be run at both component and facility level.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should consider in its frameworks for the review of estimates the availability of data for different exposure types, taking into account model architecture and existing and potential risk drivers.
quote: institutions should consider in their frameworks for the review of estimates the availability of data for different exposure types, taking into account the specificities of the model architecture

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should use complementary analyses for exposure types where quantitative measures are inconclusive because data are scarce.
quote: When data are scarce, they should use complementary analyses for those exposure types where quantitative measures prove inconclusive

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should define and put in place appropriate actions where internal data are insufficient to establish fixed targets and tolerances for metrics assessing PD model risk differentiation.
quote: Where internal data are not considered sufficient to establish fixed targets and tolerances for defined metrics and tools to assess the performance of the PD model in terms of risk differentiation, institutions should define and put in place the appropriate actions to address this.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should consider adjusting its internal data following significant changes applied to an external credit bureau score used as a main driver of the internal rating, and whenever the input variables are no longer appropriate.
quote: in cases where significant changes are applied to the credit bureau scoring institutions should consider the possibility of adjusting their internal data following the changes applied to the score

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should include in the review framework for material models with statistically based grade assignment, where slight ranking or boundary changes could significantly change RWEA, an analysis of whether including the most recent data in the RDS would lead to materially different model outcomes.
quote: the framework referred to in paragraph 328 of this chapter should also include an analysis of whether the inclusion of the most recent data in the RDS used for model development would lead to materially different model outcomes.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should conduct the analysis of the effect of the most recent RDS data on a three-yearly basis, or more often depending on the materiality of the model.
quote: This analysis should be conducted on a three-yearly basis, or more often, depending on the materiality of the model.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should consider in that analysis whether the discriminatory power of the PD or LGD models would be materially increased when re-estimating model parameters on the updated RDS.
quote: The analysis should consider, in particular, whether the discriminatory power of the PD or LGD models would be materially increased when reestimating the model parameters on the basis of the updated RDS.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should analyse individual defaults (or at least a sample where analysing all is unduly burdensome) when the number of defaults is low, to check that the main drivers of observed defaults are appropriately reflected in the model.
quote: institutions should analyse individual defaults (or at least a sample of them where the number of defaults makes analysing all of them unduly burdensome).

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should not adapt the model simply to fit singular events from its file review.
quote: the model should not be adapted simply to fit singular events from the institution's file review.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution shall document the situations in which human judgement may override the inputs or outputs of the grade and pool assignment process.
quote: for grade and pool assignments institutions must document those situations in which human judgement may override the inputs or outputs of the assignment process.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution shall complement the statistical model by human judgement and human oversight to review model-based assignments and ensure that the models are used appropriately.
quote: institutions must complement the statistical model by human judgement and human oversight to review model-based assignments and ensure that the models are used appropriately.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution shall design review procedures to find and limit errors associated with model weaknesses.
quote: review procedures must be designed to find and limit errors associated with model weaknesses.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 20.1
obligation: The institution should assess the impact of the application of human judgement on risk differentiation capability (e.g. discriminatory power).
quote: institutions should assess the impact of the application of human judgement on risk differentiation capability (e.g. on discriminatory power)

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should have internal validation policies with proven procedures and methods that adequately validate the accuracy, robustness and stability of its estimation of all relevant risk parameters.
quote: Institutions should have internal validation policies involving proven procedures and methods which adequately validate the accuracy, robustness and stability of their estimation of all relevant risk parameters.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should align the procedures and methods in its validation policy with its classification of material and non-material rating systems, also considering the complexity of the rating systems.
quote: The procedures and methods stipulated in the validation policy should be in line with the institution's classification of material and non-material rating systems

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should follow its internal validation policy when carrying out validations.
quote: Institutions should follow their internal validation policy when carrying out validations.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution shall ensure that the data used to build the model are representative of the actual obligors or exposures.
quote: The data used to build the model must be representative of the actual obligors or exposures (Article 174(c) of the CRR).

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should check that the range of application of the model is in line with the approved one, comparing obligor characteristics for PD models and facility types and characteristics for LGD and CCF models.
quote: Ensuring that the range of application of the model is in line with the approved one, in accordance with Article 143(3) of the CRR.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should monitor changes made to the definition of default to identify any that would affect the representativeness of the dataset for obligors or facilities within the model's range of application.
quote: Monitoring the changes made to the definition of default, with the aim of identifying any changes that would affect the representativeness of the dataset

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should analyse lending standards or workout procedures, external market and economic conditions, and other relevant characteristics surrounding the model development process.
quote: Analysing lending standards or workout procedures, external market and economic conditions, and other relevant characteristics surrounding the model development process.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should, where it uses data pooled across institutions, also cover the requirements of Article 179(2) paragraphs (a) and (b) of the CRR in its representativeness analyses.
quote: Where an institution uses data that are pooled across institutions, the analyses should also cover the requirements of Article 179(2) paragraphs (a) and (b) of the CRR.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should assess overrides, not only monitor them, as part of the validation process.
quote: Overrides should not only be monitored but also assessed as part of the validation process (Article 172(3) of the CRR).

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should conduct analyses of overrides on an annual basis (and not at initial validation).
quote: Analyses of overrides should be conducted on an annual basis (and not at initial validation).

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should justify excessive or unexpected variability in the stability of internal ratings and risk parameters over time.
quote: (v.b) Institutions should justify excessive or unexpected variability.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should analyse the stability of internal ratings and risk parameters over time (e.g. obligor/facility migrations, stability of the migration matrix, concentration in rating grades for PD estimates).
quote: Examples for analysing the stability of internal ratings and risk parameters over a specific observation period for PD estimates can be the following: obligor/facility migrations; stability of the migration matrix; concentration in rating grades.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should challenge the model specifications, including assumptions and methodology, based on the applicable regulation.
quote: The institution should challenge the model specifications, including assumptions and methodology, based on the applicable regulation.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should provide an overall conclusion on the model so that individual model strengths and weaknesses are evaluated on an overall basis.
quote: the validation unit should provide an overall conclusion on the model to ensure that individual model strengths and weaknesses are evaluated on an overall basis.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should analyse model design stability, including differences between original risk driver weights and weights estimated from a different (longer or more recent) sample, and the continued homogeneity of rating grades or pools used for risk parameter estimation.
quote: the differences between the original weights of the risk drivers (derived from the development sample) and the weights estimated from a different sample (longer or more recent historical sample)

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should justify excessive or unexpected variability in model specifications and design stability.
quote: (vi.b) Institutions should justify excessive or unexpected variability.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should perform model specification and design stability analyses at initial validation and at an adequate frequency thereafter, but at least as part of a full validation.
quote: These analyses should be performed at initial validation and at an adequate frequency thereafter, but at least as part of a full validation.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should evaluate input data to ensure the data treatment process is reliable and well-founded.
quote: that the data treatment process is reliable and well-founded

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should ensure that necessary information is available and up to date for the majority of the application portfolio's obligors and facilities by tracking the age of model input data, especially financial statements.
quote: that the necessary information is available and up to date for the majority of the application portfolio's 48 obligors and facilities by tracking the age of model input data, especially in the case of financial statements

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should ensure that all defaults within the model's scope of application are correctly identified and fully documented and registered in the appropriate and intended IT systems.
quote: that all defaults that occurred in the institution within the scope of application of the model are correctly identified and fully documented and registered in the appropriate and intended IT systems

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should ensure that the number and reasons for technical past-due situations are tracked.
quote: that the number and reasons for technical past-due situations are tracked.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should compare model results with up-to-date data from representative and comparable external data sources, in particular for low-default portfolios.
quote: The institution should carry out comparisons with up-to-date data from representative and comparable external data sources, in particular with regard to low-default portfolios

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should provide sufficient evidence in the event that no usable external data are available for benchmarking.
quote: The institution should provide sufficient evidence in the event that no usable external data are available.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should perform benchmarking analyses at initial validation and at an adequate frequency thereafter, but at least as part of a full validation.
quote: Benchmarking analyses should be performed at initial validation and at an adequate frequency thereafter, but at least as part of a full validation.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should perform data cleansing analyses, covering the exclusion of observations and the reasons for them from the risk database used to construct the reference dataset, at least at initial validation.
quote: These analyses should be performed at least at initial validation.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should perform quality assurance of the computer codes, including that the implementation of the rating system in the IT system is compliant with and reproduces exactly the documented model under review.
quote: that the implementation of the rating system in the relevant IT system is compliant with and reproduces exactly the documented model under review

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should check that the descriptions of the data sources, variables and risk drivers used for development are properly documented.
quote: that the descriptions of the data sources, variables and risk drivers used for development purposes are properly documented.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should perform quality assurance of the computer codes at least at initial validation.
quote: (x.b) These analyses should be performed at least at initial validation.

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The validation function should perform additional qualitative analyses, including assessment of assumptions and expert-based estimates, integrity of the rating assignment process, use of the models and their correct application in practice, legal or macroeconomic changes affecting risk parameters, and downturn phases and correct application of margins of conservatism.
quote: qualitative assessments of assumptions and expert-based estimates and of the integrity of the rating assignment process; assessment of the use of the models and their correct application in practice;

key: ECB guide to internal models, Credit risk, Section 51
obligation: The institution should have a clear policy defining the appropriate frequency of each qualitative assessment.
quote: institutions should have a clear policy in place defining the appropriate frequency of each assessment.
